title: Targeted Quality Improvement Trial to Improve Post-Discharge VTE
official: Targeted Quality Improvement Trial to Improve Post-Discharge VTE Chemoprophylaxis After Abdominal and Pelvic Cancer Surgery
summary: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is the most common preventable cause of death after major abdominal and pelvic cancer surgery, and over one-third of events occur after discharge. National guidelines recommend extended post-discharge chemoprophylaxis, but hospital adherence varies widely. This observational study has two parts. Aim 1 uses interviews, focus groups, and surveys with patients, clinicians, and health system stakeholders to identify barriers and facilitators to implementing a post-discharge VTE chemoprophylaxis quality improvement project. Aim 2 uses retrospective hospital- and population-level data and coincidence analysis to identify hospital performance phenotypes and develop targeted implementation strategies. Findings will inform a separately registered stepped-wedge implementation trial (Aim 3).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients: adults (18-85) undergoing abdominal and/or pelvic cancer surgery; English-speaking
* Clinicians: faculty and fellow physicians, advanced practice providers, physician assistants, medical assistants, dietitians, and social workers in participating surgical service clinics; English-speaking
* Stakeholders: Chief Medical Officer, Chief Information Officer, Chief Quality Officer, or related leadership

Aim 2: records of patients undergoing abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery between 1/1/2006 and 9/16/2025

Exclusion Criteria:

* Non-English-speaking individuals
* Patients not undergoing abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery
* Individuals under 18
